name: Daily Debate
tagline: Scored on evidence and rebuttal, not on winning.
summary: A daily critical-thinking app: argue a proposition against an AI opponent over at least five rounds, or head-to-head against another player with a neutral AI judge. Responses are scored on depth, evidence, logic, rebuttal and clarity.

authorship.role: Sole author — debate loop, scoring rubric, argument graph and matchmaking.
built: The five-dimension scoring rubric and per-round feedback loop
The argument graph and its grounded-evidence tests
Player-versus-player matchmaking with alternating turns over Supabase Realtime, and the neutral judge that scores the full transcript
Rate limiting and its regression tests
notBuilt: Gemini and Anthropic, which generate opponent arguments and judge transcripts
The browser Web Speech API used for dictation and read-aloud

caseStudy.problem: Debate practice needs an opponent who argues back competently and a scorer who can say why an argument was weak. Both are easy to fake badly: an AI opponent that agrees too readily teaches nothing, and a score with no rubric behind it is just a number.
caseStudy.approach: Force a minimum of five rounds so a position has to survive contact, and score every response on five named dimensions with short written feedback before the opponent replies. For head-to-head play, keep the judge neutral and score the whole transcript rather than round by round. Ground the daily topic in real, well-known institutions the user can go and research.

visuals.caption: Illustration of the debate room. Not a screenshot — no capture of the running app has been published yet.

metrics.label: Automated tests
metrics.value: 22 core plus 24 in the scoring regression suite
metrics.method: `npm test` (vitest) covering the argument graph's grounded evidence, benchmark invariance and grounding, rate limiting and gamification. Counts as stated in the project README.

outcomes.statement: The daily topic's cited institutions are presented as credible sources to go and research, not as live-fetched citations — the README states plainly that the model has no live web access in this app.

tradeoffs.choice: Naming credible institutions instead of implying live citations
tradeoffs.gained: The app never presents a fabricated link as a source, which is the standard failure of AI-generated debate prompts.
tradeoffs.gaveUp: The user has to do the research themselves; the app cannot hand them the article.

tradeoffs.choice: Voice input via the browser Web Speech API
tradeoffs.gained: Dictation and read-aloud with no service dependency and no cost.
tradeoffs.gaveUp: Chrome-family browsers only; everywhere else the composer silently falls back to typing.

limitations: Judge-scoring invariance is validated on synthetic transcripts; there is no inter-rater agreement study against human judges yet.
Rate limiting is process-local; running multiple instances would need shared state the current design does not have.
PvP assumes small trusted cohorts; anti-abuse beyond rate limits is thin.
